title: Silverpine inference usage & allocation demo
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Silverpine through the Console usage analytics and per-route cost allocation. Customer focused on multi-tenant chargeback, SSO/KMS concerns, and options to start a small dedicated pilot. Agreed to share pricing, security pack, and sample routes export for mapping.
next_steps: Rebecca - send tailored pricing sheet and Dedicated options - due 2025-10-02
Ian - share lightweight benchmark checklist and sample route-export script - due 2025-09-30
Tom - provide example per-team route list and billing mapping CSV - due 2025-10-06
Schedule pilot kick-off once Silverpine shares route CSV (proposed week of 2025-10-13)
action_items: Rebecca Lin - email security docs (SOC2 summary + VPN/VPC guide) - 2025-10-02
Ian Cho - run quick inference-perf checklist and share results template - 2025-09-30
Tom Keane - export current service routes and cost centers and share to AE - 2025-10-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-25 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Rebecca Lin (Redwood AE), Ian Cho (Redwood SE), Tom Keane (Silverpine Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Silverpine SRE), Luis Martinez (Silverpine FinOps)

[00:00] Rebecca: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:03] Tom: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Rebecca.
[00:06] Rebecca: Awesome. So, goal for today — give you a focused tour of the Console around per-route usage, cost allocation, and the controls we use in Redwood Optimize to reduce token spend. Ian will jump into the more technical bits later.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good, we're particularly interested in how we can map routes back to our internal cost centers and what the SSO/KMS story is.
[00:28] Rebecca: Great - we'll cover that. Quick context check from your side, Tom? Are you running most traffic through hosted, or self-hosted / private?
[00:35] Tom: Right now it's a mix. Core customer-facing chat flows are on a managed endpoint with another provider, some internal teams are experimenting with on-prem GPUs. Our biggest pain is line-item allocation — we can't tell which feature consumed what tokens unless we do heavy logging.
[00:49] Luis: And for FinOps it's impossible to reconcile across teams. We want to do per-team chargeback by route or by service.
[00:56] Rebecca: Totally — that's exactly where Console's per-route dashboards and the route tagging come in. I'll share my screen and walk through a sandbox account so you can see the mapping.
[01:10] [screen shares]
[01:18] Rebecca: Ok, on the left is the Usage tab. Top-level you get total tokens, mean latency, and then the breakdown by route. We automatically cluster by route path, but you can also upload a custom route map.
[01:35] Priya: Quick question — clustering sometimes lumps admin calls together for us. Can we force a regex mapping?
[01:40] Ian: Yes, you can create a custom route map — we support regex and explicit matching. The Console will then re-aggregate past data against that map. There's a small reprocessing window for large exports but it's lightweight.
[01:55] Rebecca: Here's an example: we split /api/chat/assistant.v2 into three routes for dev/prod/experiment using labels. See the cost column — that's normalized per 1k tokens and also shown as actual spend.
[02:10] Tom: The cost math — is that derived from your hosted per-token pricing or can we plug our own costs for Dedicated?
[02:15] Ian: You can set a cost profile per deployment. For hosted it uses Redwood's published unit economics; for Dedicated or Private you can define per-GPU cost plus operational overhead, or simply set a per-token cost to match your internal billing.
[02:30] Luis: Nice. What about quantization differences — we run some models in FP16 and some quantized int8, will the Console show the resulting cost delta?
[02:38] Ian: We try to surface model variant cost impacts. If the model variant exposes throughput or token cost metadata, Console will break it out. It's not magic — you need to register the variant and associate routes with that variant, then the per-route view will show both token counts and effective unit cost. There can be subtlety with K-V cache hits.
[02:56] Priya: Sorry, you said K-V cash? I heard K-V cash earlier — is that the KV cache?
[03:01] Ian: Yeah, KV cache. Sorry the mic cut. KV cache hits reduce compute overhead; we show cache hit rates per-route so you can see where you might be double-counting tokens vs compute.
[03:12] Rebecca: Moving along — here is the per-route timeline; you can zoom to any date range and pivot by model, deployment, or team tag. You can also export a CSV that lists token buckets per route so your internal billing system can ingest it.
[03:28] Tom: Do you have an API for pulling route-level metrics?
[03:31] Rebecca: Yep — the Usage API supports route_id, team_tag, model, and a window. We'll send the API doc link.
[03:37] Priya: On compliance — we need audit logs for token access and who restarted which model. How deep are those logs?
[03:44] Ian: Audit logs cover deployment changes, route map uploads, token-level anomalies, and user activity (SSO events). For Private deployments you can forward logs to your SIEM or set up a push to an S3/GCS bucket. We also have optional HSM/KMS key integration for token encryption at rest.
[03:58] Luis: Is Redwood SOC2 certified?
[04:01] Rebecca: Yes, plus we publish a compliance pack — we'll attach the SOC2 summary and our pen test overview.
[04:08] Tom: Great. Show us an example of allocation — say a rule where messages with metadata X get billed to team B.
[04:15] [screen navigate]
[04:18] Ian: Alright, in the route settings you can define a mapping rule: match header X-Feature:rewrites -> allocate to cost center 'rewrite-team'. We then apply this mapping to historic traffic; you can preview the allocation before committing.
[04:33] Luis: Does that work with downstream function calls or tool calling? Some of our flows fan out to 2-3 tool calls per user request.
[04:41] Ian: The Console treats tool calls as sub-requests and attributes them to the parent route unless you explicitly split them. You can annotate tool calls in the SDK so they show up under their own route if needed.
[04:54] Priya: Hmm ok. Back to Dedicated vs Hosted routing — if we start with hosted but later move to Dedicated for high-throughput routes, can we keep the same route IDs for continuity?
[05:05] Rebecca: Yes, route IDs are logical — you can pin a route to a deployment, and switching the underlying deployment keeps the route and the historical metrics intact. We also support canary routing and fallback: if Dedicated is saturated we can spill to hosted with an alternate variant.
[05:21] Tom: Any limits on retention for the route-level granularity? We need 12 months for finance.
[05:26] Ian: Out of the box we keep 13 months with aggregated daily rollups and 90 days of high-resolution request traces. For longer retention you can buy extended retention or configure exports to your S3.
[05:39] Rebecca: Let me demonstrate a quick cost-breakdown widget — this one shows top 10 routes by spend, with per-token cost, tokens consumed, and estimated monthly run rate. You can click a route and see associated labels and the last 5 deploys that touched it.
[05:55] [clicks]
[05:58] Luis: That monthly run rate helps. For forecasting, can we plug our internal discount for committed Dedicated capacity?
[06:05] Ian: Yes, in the cost profile you can add committed discount factors and reserved capacity parameters; the forecast will then show both on-demand and committed scenarios.
[06:16] Tom: Ok, let's talk about a pilot. We want to try a small Dedicated pool for our high-volume /api/chat/prod route and route most other stuff hosted. How would you recommend sizing?
[06:26] Ian: We'll need your qps and average token length distribution. For quick sizing we have a heuristic in the Console's Optimize tab: you upload a sample of your traffic, it suggests batch sizes, GPU types, and whether INT8 quantization is recommended. We can run that on a 24h sample and come back with an estimated Dedicated vCPU/GPU footprint.
[06:45] Priya: Are there any stability tradeoffs with aggressive batching? Some of our product SLOs are 200ms p95.
[06:52] Ian: Batching reduces cost but increases tail latency. Our Optimize engine simulates latency distribution for given batch/window configs. For 200ms p95 you might need small batches + KV caching. We'll show you a sample simulation.
[07:04] Rebecca: I'll highlight the Optimize recommendations and the 'safe defaults' toggle which auto-configures per-route batching thresholds to keep p95 under your target while still saving cost.
[07:15] Tom: Looks promising. A few nitty gritty Qs — can route-level RBAC prevent some teams from seeing other teams' token counts? We need least-privilege.
[07:24] Ian: Yes, Console supports RBAC at the route and team level. You can scope access to route groups and mask sensitive columns if needed. We'll include the RBAC doc.
[07:33] Priya: For Private deployments, do you still get the Console UI or is that self-hosted?
[07:38] Rebecca: You get the same Console but with a private control plane. Metadata and audit logs can be stored in your VPC. There's an on-prem package if you need air-gapped operation.
[07:48] Luis: Any surprises on network egress? We need to keep egress minimum for EU customers.
[07:53] Ian: For Private deployments everything stays in your VPC so egress is internal. For Dedicated hosted in our region we can provision in EU zones to minimize cross-border egress.
[08:04] Tom: Okay, can you run through an example export for FinOps? I want columns we can import into our chargeback system.
[08:11] [screen]
[08:14] Rebecca: Export includes: timestamp, route_id, route_name, team_tag, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, unit_cost, billed_amount, request_id. You can add custom metadata columns if you send them as headers.
[08:28] Luis: Great. We'll want a sample CSV to try mapping.
[08:31] Rebecca: We'll attach a sample.
[08:33] Priya: About the API rate limits — if we poll Usage API every minute for dashboards, is there a recommended pattern?
[08:40] Ian: We recommend a push model for near real-time (webhooks) or a cached export every 5 minutes. Polling every minute is fine for small teams but for large ingest we suggest exports into S3 and then you run your internal pipelines.
[08:53] Tom: On the model registry side — if we version models frequently, does Console tie metrics to specific model commits?
[08:59] Ian: You can tag deploys with a git sha or model hash. Deploy history shows the sha, and you can compare metrics across deploys. This is useful for regressions in quality or token usage.
[09:10] Rebecca: Switching gears to security again — we heard you mention KMS. For Private deployments, we integrate with customer-managed keys. For hosted, we use managed keys but can support bring-your-own-key via HSM for enterprise plans.
[09:25] Luis: Any latency penalty with HSM?
[09:28] Ian: Minimal for key unwrap operations; runtime signing is local to the node. HSM latency isn't on the per-token path except for key rotation events.
[09:37] [pause, notes being recorded]
[09:45] Tom: Can we see an example of a route-level anomaly alert? We get sudden token spikes from a feature rollouts and we need to detect these quickly.
[09:54] Rebecca: Sure. I'll open Alerts. You can set thresholds on token rate, sudden delta, or p95 latency. Alerts can be routed to Slack, PagerDuty, or email and include a snapshot link to the last 5 minutes of traces.
[10:08] Priya: Does the alerting detect when a route has high tool-call fanout?
[10:12] Ian: You can write composite alerts that look at number of downstream calls per request. We also provide anomaly detection that learns baseline fanout per route and alerts on deviation.
[10:23] Tom: Good. Onboarding — how long before we can get a pilot live?
[10:27] Rebecca: Onboarding for a small pilot is usually 2-3 weeks: security review + test data agreement in week 1, integrations and route mapping week 2, and pilot validation week 3. If you choose Dedicated and need hardware procurement it may add time.
[10:40] Luis: Budget-wise, what should we expect for a small Dedicated pool?
[10:44] Ian: Rough ballpark depends on GPU type. For example a single A10G-class instance as Dedicated for low-latency inference can start at X/month; we'll provide real numbers in the pricing sheet. We also offer short-term reserved pricing if you commit 3-6 months which reduces unit cost substantially.
[10:59] Tom: Are there trial credits for us to run the Optimize flow?
[11:02] Rebecca: Yes — we'll allocate a small eval credit to run a 24h sample through Optimize and produce recommendations.
[11:09] [screen: Optimize tab]
[11:12] Ian: Here is the sample optimize run — it analyzed token distribution and recommended batch size 8 for model v2-small, and a 12% cost reduction if you enable prefix KV caching for the top three routes. The report shows expected p95 change and cost delta.
[11:30] Priya: How reliable are those savings? Sometimes our workloads are bursty.
[11:34] Ian: The recommendations are data-driven from your sample; for bursty workloads we suggest conservative batch windows and enable autoscaling with burst capacity so you don't impact SLOs.
[11:46] Tom: Any examples of customers who moved the high-volume chat to Dedicated and saved money?
[11:51] Rebecca: Yes, a marketplace customer cut per-token cost 38% by moving a high-volume route to Dedicated with INT8 quantization and KV caching. We can anonymize the case study and share it.
[12:02] Luis: Please do. That will help procurement.
[12:07] Rebecca: Quick note on integration complexity — SDKs are available for JS, Python, and Go. We have a sample route-export script that transforms platform route names into Console route IDs. Ian, show the mapping script?
[12:19] Ian: Sure. In the SDK you can annotate each request with route_id and team_tag. We also provide middleware for common frameworks that auto-instrument routes. It takes a few hours to wire up, depending on your stack.
[12:32] [screen shows code snippet with a small typo in variable names — customers laugh]
[12:36] Tom: That looks straightforward. Final questions from our side: latency SLOs for region EU-west, and SLA uptime on Dedicated?
[12:45] Ian: For EU-west we can provision nodes in region with p95 in the low 100s for small models; Dedicated SLAs are in the enterprise contract — 99.9% availability with defined repair windows. We'll route you to the contract team for exact SLA wording.
[13:02] Rebecca: We're approaching two-thirds of the call time — want to do a quick recap and next steps?
[13:08] Tom: Yes please.
[13:10] Rebecca: Recap: 1) Console supports per-route dashboards, custom route maps, exports for FinOps; 2) Optimize suggests batching, KV caching, and quantization options with simulated latency/cost tradeoffs; 3) Security: SOC2, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; 4) Pilot path: small Dedicated for high-volume route + hosted for rest. Next steps: we'll send pricing, security docs, sample CSV, and the Optimize trial credits.
[13:35] Priya: Sounds good. Also, we'll send you the route CSV by Oct 6.
[13:40] Rebecca: Perfect. Anything else?
[13:42] Luis: One last thing — competitor question: how do you compare to Anthropic on cost transparency?
[13:47] Rebecca: We focus on route-level economics and transparent per-token + deployment cost profiles; other vendors may show token counts but not the deployment-level economics or dedicated cost profiles the same way. We'll include a short comparison doc.
[13:58] Tom: Thanks all.
[14:00] Rebecca: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up.

[End of transcript — remaining 33 minutes were Q&A and follow-up clarifications captured in meeting notes and exported artifacts.]
